summary.en: Post-punk and garage guitar bands reclaim radio after nu-metal and laptop pop.
summary.zh: 后朋克与车库吉他乐队在 Nu-Metal 与笔记本流行乐之后重占电台。

sound.en: Tight garage snare, post-punk eighth-note bass, three-minute singles, dry room mics, White Stripes-style minimal guitar+drums, Strokes NYC compression
sound.zh: 紧 Garage 军鼓、后朋克八分贝斯、三分钟单曲、干房间话筒、White Stripes 式极简吉他+鼓、Strokes 纽约压缩感

body.en:
By 2000–01 US/UK charts lean on nu-metal and early digital pop. New York’s The Strokes put Is This It (2001) on MTV and indie press: three-minute songs, clipped vocals, dry garage drums. The White Stripes keep two-piece garage (guitar/drums, limited bass) visible on White Blood Cells (2001) and Elephant (2003).

Interpol’s Turn On the Bright Lights (2002) and Franz Ferdinand’s debut (2004) export post-punk bass and danceable guitar to UK/US radio. Arctic Monkeys’ Whatever People Say I Am… (2006) shows MySpace and UK indie weeklies can break a Sheffield guitar band into the singles chart within months.

Festival bills (Reading, Coachella, Glastonbury) pull the same lean guitar acts onto large stages. Parallel US paths—Killers synth-rock, Fall Out Boy pop-punk—share the decade’s radio space without sharing the NYC/UK garage press frame.
body.zh:
2000–01 年美英榜单偏 Nu-Metal 与早期数字流行。纽约 The Strokes 把《Is This It》（2001）送上 MTV 与独立媒体：三分钟歌、短促人声、干车库鼓。The White Stripes 在《White Blood Cells》（2001）与《Elephant》（2003）上保持二人编制车库（吉他/鼓、贝斯极简）。

Interpol《Turn On the Bright Lights》（2002）与 Franz Ferdinand 首专（2004）把后朋克贝斯与可跳舞吉他送进英美电台。Arctic Monkeys《Whatever People Say I Am…》（2006）证明 MySpace 与英国独立周刊能在数月内把谢菲尔德吉他乐队打进单曲榜。

Reading、Coachella、Glastonbury 等音乐节把同一批精简吉他乐队拉上大舞台。并行的美国路线——Killers 合成器摇滚、Fall Out Boy 流行朋克——共享电台时段，但不共用纽约/英国车库媒体框架。
